tools.name: search-directory
tools.description: Search the Noonlaunch product directory. Returns approved products matching the query, ordered by community votes, with links to their Noonlaunch product pages.

tools.name: get-product
tools.description: Get full public details of one Noonlaunch product by its slug (the last part of its noonlaunch.com/product/... URL).

tools.name: get-weekly-winners
tools.description: Get the Noonlaunch launch board for a week: the top-voted free launches, with the top 3 marked as winners. weeks_ago 0 is the current (still running) week, 1 is the last completed week.

tools.name: list-launch-directories
tools.description: Browse Noonlaunch's curated list of 333 startup launch directories and communities where founders can submit a product. Filterable by category, cost and minimum domain authority.

tools.name: get-plans
tools.description: What it costs to launch on Noonlaunch, and what each plan includes. Use this to answer a pricing question on its own. To actually submit a product, call check_product instead: which plans apply depends on the site, because relaunching one that is already listed needs a paid plan.

tools.name: check-product
tools.description: Check whether a product can be submitted to Noonlaunch, and get the plans, categories and launch weeks available for it. Always call this first, and always ask the person for their live public website URL rather than guessing it from their code.

tools.name: submit-product
tools.description: Submit a product to Noonlaunch. Nothing is published by this call. It returns a claim link to give the person straight away. Free launches are reviewed by an admin; nothing needs installing. Call check_product first.

tools.name: verify-badge
tools.description: No longer needed: the Noonlaunch badge is optional and free launches are reviewed by an admin. This returns the listing status. Use check_status instead.

tools.name: check-status
tools.description: Where a submission stands: whether it has been claimed, paid for, verified and published. This is the only way to find out whether a payment has landed. Poll it rather than assuming.

tools.name: report-badge-problem
tools.description: No longer needed: the Noonlaunch badge is optional, so there is no badge check to report. Use check_status to follow a listing.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get-product, check-product · Public sink: list-launch-directories, get-plans, submit-product.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get-product, check-product · Public sink: list-launch-directories, get-plans, submit-product

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "submit-product" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Submit a product to Noonlaunch. Nothing is published by this call. It returns a claim link to give the person straight away, and for free launches the badge snippet to install. Call check_product first." → after: "Submit a product to Noonlaunch. Nothing is published by this call. It returns a claim link to give the person straight away. Free launches are reviewed by an admin; nothing needs installing. Call check_product first."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
